title: Early pay in New Orleans and Raceland
summary: Punch recalls his first New Orleans job pay and playing for tips on a store gallery in Raceland.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Well what about the pay in all these different years? How was the pay down here in New Orleans when you first started?
What do you mean pay money?
Well let me see, I believe the first job I got in New Orleans I got something like two and a half with Jack Kerber.
Now before that in Raceland would you make any money?

Oh yeah we'd make, like, me and this boy they called Lonnie Johnson now, we called him Rooster at home, but we'd play on Saturday evening on a big store gallery you see, and put our hat down and all the people that's playing put money in our hat see, we didn't have no siren or nothing like that. But when we got through, that Saturday and that Saturday night, that Saturday evening and that Saturday night, we ain't gonna have enough money to lend us all that next week. See? Yeah.
Just play that one day and you'd have enough to make it all.

Saturday, it's all day Saturday and Saturday night and we might play a little guitar, bass and trumpet outfit for something about white folks you know on Sunday night like that. But how much would that pay? Well that pay us like about two dollars a man.
How much would you get for those tips on Saturday?
Oh, them tips run around about fifteen dollars, something like that. That'll last a long time.
